prerequisites: EM1012 - Mechanics of Machines and Structures
EM1019 - Elasticity and Strength of Materials
EM1020 - Theory of Machines and Mechanisms

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to work in a team to prepare the review and certification documents for a machine or installation.
Be able to prepare a review protocol for a fluid mechanical installation.
Be able to prepare a review protocol for a thermal installation or machine.
Be able to prepare a review protocol for a machine.
Be able to analyze and synthesize the applicable regulations for the review and certification of a machine or installation.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Industry Law. General framework of activities. Ordinances.
Topic 2: Commercial and industrial installations. Control bodies.
Topic 3: Reviews and certificates regarding fire in buildings. CTE.
Topic 4: Reviews and certificates regarding fire in industrial installations.
Topic 5: Reviews and certificates in low voltage installations. REBT.
Topic 6: Reviews and certificates in thermal installations in buildings.
Topic 7: Reviews and certificates for chemical product storage installations. APQs.
Topic 8: Reviews and certificates for pressure vessels. REP.
Topic 9: CE marking: machines, personal protective equipment.
Analysis of practical cases in relation to: The agents involved in the review of an installation.
Analysis of practical cases in relation to: The structure of applicable technical standards.
Analysis of practical cases in relation to: Accidents related to fire, in public access premises (CTE) and industrial establishments (RSCIEI).
Analysis of practical cases in relation to: Reviews of thermal equipment in buildings.
Single submission: review and presentation of an industrial safety regulation concerning mandatory reviews.
assessment_rules: Students will pass the course if they obtain at least 5 out of 10 points in the weighted overall grade. For the first attempt, continuous assessment (40%) has no minimum grade, but the final exam (60%) requires a minimum of 4 out of 10. If the final exam minimum is not met, the overall weighted grade cannot exceed 4.5 out of 10. For the second attempt, continuous assessment (40%) grade is maintained unless recovered, and the final exam (60%) still requires a minimum of 4 out of 10, with the same overall grade cap of 4.5 if the minimum is not met. In the extraordinary final attempt, the final exam accounts for 100% with no minimum grade. Laboratory practical reports can be recovered in the second attempt by submitting a corrected, expanded, or completed version; this recovery only affects the documentation, not the practical sessions.
